This looks like a CBP ruling on a receiver (liquid receiver) for an HVAC system. Candidate headings are 8419.90 (parts of heat-exchange equipment), 8418.99 (parts of refrigerating equipment), and 7311 (containers for compressed gas, of iron or steel).

Heading 7311 covers containers for compressed or liquefied gas of iron or steel. Rulings on refrigerant receivers have gone both ways. The container has no valves or mechanical parts, and it is a steel cylinder that holds pressurized liquid refrigerant. A 3.4-liter capacity falls under 7311.00.00, which is split by capacity into 7311.00.30 (under 1,000 cu cm), 7311.00.60 (1,000 cu cm or more, 7311.00.60 for 1,000 cu cm or more), and 7311.00.0060.

The HTSUS 7311.00 subheadings are:
- 7311.00.00: containers for compressed or liquefied gas, of iron or steel
- 7311.00.30: seamless
- 7311.00.60: other, with further splits by capacity and type

Within 7311.00.60, the statistical suffixes are 7311.00.6000 and so on. I recall the structure as 7311.00.30 (Seamless: 00 Other...), 7311.00.60 (Welded, 30 or 90...), and the 7311.00.00 line with 7311.00.0030 for capacity under 1.05 liters. The 3.4-liter size does not fit that smallest bracket.

I believe the structure is 7311.00.00 with 7311.00.0030 for seamless, 7311.00.0060 for welded and under 1.05 L, and 7311.00.0090 for others. I will go with 7311.00.6000 as the best guess for a steel pressurized container of this capacity, since the capacity split in the tariff is "having a capacity of less than 1,000 cc" versus "1,000 cc or more".

Weighing the options, I will choose 7311.00.6000.
